title: Simple and Compound Interest
shortDescription: SI, CI, annual/half-yearly compounding, difference formulas and growth rules.
genZNote: SI is a straight line; CI is a snowball. Know the 2-year difference shortcut and half-yearly switch and you're done.

sections.heading: Simple Interest
bullets: SI = P × R × T / 100; Amount A = P + SI.
Time for money to become k times at SI: T = (k − 1) × 100 / R. Doubling at 10% takes 10 years.

sections.heading: Compound Interest
bullets: Half-yearly: rate R/2, periods 2n. Quarterly: R/4, 4n.
Different rates for successive years: A = P(1 + r₁)(1 + r₂)…
Rule of 72: doubling time ≈ 72 / R (years) at compound rate R%.

sections.heading: CI − SI Shortcuts
bullets: For 3 years: CI − SI = P(r)²(3 + r) with r = R/100.
Equal annual instalments and loans: treat with present-value discounting; if CI and SI are given for 2 years, SI per year = SI/2 and rate = (CI − SI) / (SI/2) × 100.
Population growth, depreciation and bacteria use the same compound formula (depreciation uses 1 − R/100).

quickRevision.oneLineDefinition: Simple interest grows linearly on principal; compound interest grows on principal plus accumulated interest.

highYieldFacts: CI for year 1 equals SI for year 1.
commonTraps: Do not forget to halve the rate and double the time for half-yearly.

sources.name: Standard quantitative aptitude reference (R.S. Aggarwal, Quantitative Aptitude)
